item.title: Skip link: jump straight past the menu.
item.description:
Word of the day: Skip link: jump straight past the menu.
A link at the very top of the page that takes keyboard and screen reader users straight to the main content. It is one way to meet WCAG 2.4.1, Bypass Blocks, at Level A.
Spot it: Load your page and press Tab once. The first thing that appears should be a way to skip to the content.

item.title: Amnesty's robots.txt turns Bingbot away.
item.description:
Preloaded HSTS, a content security policy, and pages that name their language. But robots.txt disallows bingbot from the whole site, and Bing's index also feeds Copilot. PerplexityBot is blocked too.
The lesson for every team: Audit robots.txt line by line. Blocking a search crawler removes you from every product built on its index.

item.title: The Guardian front page has no h1.
item.description:

The lesson for every team: Give every page one h1 that names it, even a visually hidden one on a front page. Headings are how many people navigate.

item.title: Can anyone send mail as your domain?
item.description:
30-second trick: Can anyone send mail as your domain?
A DMARC record tells receiving servers what to do with mail that claims your domain but fails authentication. Without one, spoofed mail has an easier way in.
Try it now: Run the lookup on your domain. No answer? Publish p=none with a report address, read the reports, then move to quarantine.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=dmarc

item.description:

The lesson for every team: Read the reports for a few weeks, fix what they flag, then switch the header to Content-Security-Policy.

item.title: MSF serves every page without HSTS.
item.description:
Pages name their language, Arabic included with right-to-left set, and a sitemap answers. But none of the 20 pages analyzed sends Strict-Transport-Security, so a first visit over http can be intercepted.
The lesson for every team: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. Then consider the browser preload list.

This week in web quality, Nov 13, 2026
Five picks from our daily sweep of the field, each summed up in our own words and credited to its source.
1. Lighthouse 13.6 can lift your PSI score PageSpeed Insights now runs Lighthouse 13.6, which changes how it simulates FCP and LCP. Chrome's Barry Pollard says scores usually come out higher, most often on JavaScript-heavy sites, even when the page did not change. Before crediting a better score to your own work, check that both reports name the same Lighthouse version and compare the field data. By Matt G. Southern, Search Engine Journal: https://www.searchenginejournal.com/pagespeed-insights-scores-lighthouse-update/595698/
2. Playwright 1.65 runs tests under Bun Playwright 1.65 runs its test runner under Bun with bunx --bun playwright test, without watch mode. A new failures reporter and an onlyFailures option keep reports to what went wrong. Among the breaking changes, actions now wait for an inert element to stop being inert, and Node.js 20 is no longer tested. By dgozman, Playwright releases: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.65.0
3. Google on 301s, 302s and ranking signals Google's Gary Illyes and Cherry Prommawin explained that a 301 hands the old URL's ranking signals to the new one, while a 302 keeps the old URL in results because Google expects it back. A 307 or 308 does the same jobs but keeps form data on a POST. They recommend server-side redirects over JavaScript or meta refresh. By Roger Montti, Search Engine Journal: https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-explains-how-redirects-affect-ranking-signals/595967/
4. Reporting SEO when GA4 sees less After a stricter consent policy, GA4 organic sessions fell 64% in four weeks while Search Console clicks rose 1.8%. Dii Pooler shows how to audit where tracking stops, compare GA4 with backend records, and report search visibility, tracked behavior and verified outcomes separately, with the measurement limits stated first. By Dii Pooler, Moz: https://moz.com/blog/measure-seo-performance-incomplete-data
5. AI can check an ACR, not write it Will Creedle argues that general AI tools cannot test, fix or assess WCAG conformance on their own, so they should not produce a VPAT-based Accessibility Conformance Report alone. They do help catch errors, such as a wrong EN 301 549 clause or not evaluated in place of not applicable, and make the wording clearer. By Will Creedle, Deque: https://www.deque.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-vpat-approach-for-your-organization/

item.title: LCP: when the main thing shows up.
item.description:
Word of the day: LCP: when the main thing shows up.
Largest Contentful Paint marks when the biggest image or text block in the viewport finishes rendering. Good is 2.5 seconds or less for at least 75% of page loads.
Spot it: Open the Performance panel in Chrome DevTools: its live metrics name your LCP element. Make sure it is never lazy-loaded.

item.title: UNICEF's date filter has no label.
item.description:
Preloaded HSTS, Organization JSON-LD, and five language versions linked to each other. But the search date filter on every page analyzed is named only by placeholder text, which vanishes as you type.
The lesson for every team: Give every field a <label> or an aria-label. A placeholder is a hint, not a name, and it disappears on input.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-100-2026-11&utm_content=unicef

item.title: The World Bank: GEO 97.
item.description:
Organization JSON-LD with a site search action, a sitemap, robots.txt open to every crawler, and two-year HSTS. What it lacks is a content security policy: none of the pages analyzed sends one.
The lesson for every team: Start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only to see what would break, then enforce. default-src 'self' is a start.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-100-2026-11&utm_content=worldbank

item.title: 808ball16.com: 53. The gap: button names.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But buttons must have discernible text.
The lesson for every team: Give every button text or an aria-label, so a screen reader can announce it.
